sizeNote: 31 entries. Every entry carries a derivation chain terminating at Tier-0 (UCL-D01). A concept whose chain cannot be stated cannot be registered as canonical (UCL-D03).

concepts.name: Entity
concepts.statement: An existent apprehensible as one thing.

concepts.name: Identity
concepts.statement: A distinction of an entity preserved across change.

concepts.name: Reality
concepts.statement: The class of existents whose distinction does not depend on any particular model.

concepts.name: Relationship
concepts.statement: An identifiable relation between two or more entities.

concepts.name: Attribute
concepts.statement: A typed, named axis along which entities are distinguished.

concepts.name: State
concepts.statement: The complete set of an entity's attribute-values at one position in an ordering.

concepts.name: Event
concepts.statement: A transition between states, apprehended as one occurrence.

concepts.name: Time
concepts.statement: The ordering induced by change.

concepts.name: Space
concepts.statement: The ordering induced by co-existent distinction — the manifold of alongside.

concepts.name: Classification
concepts.statement: The act or result of grouping entities by shared attribute-values.

concepts.name: Taxonomy
concepts.statement: A connected system of classifications ordered by distinction-refinement.

concepts.name: Capability
concepts.statement: An entity's power to cause change in a specified way.

concepts.name: Action
concepts.statement: An exercised capability of a purposeful entity.

concepts.name: Constraint
concepts.statement: The exclusion of possibilities. (Tier-0 primitive FR-05 restated for reference.)

concepts.name: Rule
concepts.statement: A constraint expressed as a conditional over states and actions.

concepts.name: Policy
concepts.statement: A purpose-bearing, context-relative, authority-issued body of rules and objectives.

concepts.name: Context
concepts.statement: The relevant situation within which an evaluation is made; relevance is purpose-relative.

concepts.name: Lifecycle
concepts.statement: The policy-governed set of states an entity may traverse, and the admissible transitions among them.

concepts.name: Resource
concepts.statement: An entity whose capability is scarce relative to a purpose.

concepts.name: Value
concepts.statement: A purpose-relative magnitude of preference attributed to an entity or state in a context.

concepts.name: Measurement
concepts.statement: The assignment of a symbolic magnitude to a distinction-axis by comparison to a unit under a stated method.

concepts.name: Knowledge
concepts.statement: A justified, contextualised apprehension of existents, held such that it can ground action.

concepts.name: Meaning
concepts.statement: The relation between a representation and that which it is about, as established in a context.

concepts.name: Decision
concepts.statement: The selection of one alternative over others by a purposeful authority.

concepts.name: Intelligence
concepts.statement: The purposeful application of knowledge to select and execute actions that move states toward objectives.

concepts.name: Trust
concepts.statement: A justified expectation that another entity will act within a stated constraint.

concepts.name: Certification
concepts.statement: A registered, verifiable claim that an artifact satisfies a stated standard, issued by an authority separate from its owner.

concepts.name: Evolution
concepts.statement: Change applied to the descriptive layer, preserving referential integrity.

concepts.name: Governance
concepts.statement: The system of authorities, constraints, and decisions that governs action within a scope.

concepts.name: Contract
concepts.statement: A mutually binding specification of expected behaviour between two authorities.

concepts.name: Evidence
concepts.statement: An artifact that justifies a claim, sufficient to ground trust or certification.

ORDERING.statement: Time is the ordering along which a single entity's distinctions differ; Space is the ordering along which distinct entities are simultaneously present. One primitive, two readings. Interval and region are the same structure; a schedule and a capacity plan are the same structure; a booking and a spatial reservation are the same object (Phase 006).

weightBearers.note: Three derivations carry disproportionate architectural weight.
weightBearers.spaceTime: Derived from Distinction + Change jointly — removes an entire duplicated subsystem most platforms build twice.
weightBearers.value: Value = Purpose + Measurement + Context. No entity has a value; an entity has a value for a purpose in a context. This is why pricing is a relationship, never a field (Phase 006).
weightBearers.resource: Requires scarcity relative to a purpose. Air is not a resource until a purpose makes its scarcity relevant. Resource is a role, not a type (Phase 003).

oneQuestionAudit.instructions: Pick any construct. Ask: from what more fundamental concept is this derived? Recurse. Termination at a Tier-0 primitive = sound. 'It just is' = violation. A domain noun (order, invoice, patient, listing) = the construct has escaped the ontology and must be re-derived.
